summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The four calls stay neutral with low conviction while the market's trend leans down. Nothing here is expected to beat the index or is something to buy; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The brain looked at its runners again. Picking the strong-looking ones did no better than pulling names from a hat in old races, so it keeps watching with pretend money. The family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing changes. The weekly buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual for money we will leave alone for years, and money we may need soon stays safe. A market leaning down for a while is ordinary weather.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stands at one week won and one lost, and this week's bet is a little ahead so far. A coin would do the same; a few weeks prove nothing.

Third, a lesson. Last week the chart checklist turned against two of our names; this week it turned back, with nothing new in the businesses. If a signal flips every few days, it is telling us about mood, not value. Microsoft reports today, and one report can swing a stock either way, which is why we never bet real money on one.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
